title: L1 Capstone: Your Personal Toolbox
story: You've mastered functions! Fifty lessons ago, you couldn't write a single line of XIOM. Now you have a complete toolbox — math functions, string manipulators, Boolean checkers, random generators, void procedures. Every tool you've built is ready to use. This is your graduation project: assemble them all into one magnificent showcase.
why: This capstone synthesizes all L1 function patterns into a single comprehensive program — proving that real applications are built by composing many small, well-designed functions orchestrated from main().
analogy: Your personal toolbox is like a master craftsman's workshop at the end of an apprenticeship. On the wall hang: the factorial wrench (math), the reverse screwdriver (strings), the palindrome level (booleans), the dice roller (random), the fortune cookie machine (generators). Each tool was forged in a different lesson. Together they form a complete set — ready for any project that comes through the door. The workshop (main) is organized, labeled, and ready for visitors.
try_it: Add a ninth function to your toolbox — something completely original that you design from scratch. Ideas: `fibonacci(n) -> Int`, `temperature_convert(celsius: Int) -> Int`, `password_strength(pw: Str) -> Str`, `day_of_week_name(num: Int) -> Str`. Name your function, write it, and call it from the showcase.
tips: Organize your showcase with section headers: Math Tools, String Tools, Boolean Tools, Random Tools
Each function should be callable independently — test them one at a time before the full showcase
Use descriptive output in main() so someone reading the code understands what each call does
The patterns you've learned (accumulator, two-pointer, if/elif chain, random select) are the building blocks of all software
common_mistakes: Writing one giant function instead of many small ones — the capstone is about composition
Forgetting to call all functions from main() — an uncalled function is invisible
Mixing categories — keep math logic in math functions, string logic in string functions
Skipping error handling — factorial(-5) and is_palindrome("") should still work correctly
